title: LE,NONET Preparation Seminar
description: Introduces Indigenous (First Nations, Métis, Inuit, non-status) students to knowledge and skills necessary for working with Indigenous communities and organizations, or with campus-based academic researchers, through a Research Apprenticeship or Community Internship. Provides an introduction to Western and Indigenous research methodologies.
notes: Credit will be granted for only one of IS 310D, IS 220, IS 310, 310A, IS 310B.
recommendations: One of IS 101, IS 201, CYC 230, GNDR 203, POLI 263, ANTH 201, SOCI 103 recommended prior to IS 310D.
LE,NONET courses are reserved for Indigenous students.
